clues: This has existed as a signaling molecule in single-celled organisms, plants, fungi, and invertebrate species like worms and sea slugs for over 700 million years. In insect venoms, it primarily acts as an irritant designed to maximize pain, accelerate venom circulation, and incapacitate predators or prey

In the human body, more than 90% of this is produced and stored in the gut by enterochromaffin cells and was first discovered there as 'enteramine'. It's also found in the brain and converted into melatonin every night.

Tryptophan is converted into this substance (also known as 5-hydroxytryptamine or 5-HT) but relies heavily on light. Sunlight triggers the enzyme tryptophan hydroxylase, accelerating the conversion process. This can be why some people experience Seasonal Affective Disorder during dark winter months with production of this sustance drops
One of the earliest written accounts of this comes from China in 2000BC, believing it was a spiritual sign that a person's life force was actively slipping away

In the 19th century, this was viewed as a form of biological insanity and was known as 'delirium cordis', believing that the affected organ had lost its sanity and was functioning without rhyme or reason
Up to 30-40% of Caucasian adults will develop this during their lifetime. It causes up to 25-35% of all strokes, yet many people can be asymptomatic

Ancient Chinese texts like the Pen Ts'ao documented over 1,000 herbal remedies for this condition, including mallow and white peony root. Before the 19th century, doctors also tried bloodletting, cupping, leeches, and herbal enemas
Cranberries contain compounds called proanthocyanidins, which can help prevent recurrence of this disease but does not treat it.
Approximately 50-60% of women will experience this in their lifetime. Most cases are caused by E. Coli
Some medical historians believe that this disease may have killed Alexander the Great. He died at the age of 34 after a night of heavy drinking and overeating in Babylon

In October 1965, US President Lyndon B Johnson underwent a procedure to treat this condition. To quell conspiracy theories and rumors regarding his health, during a press conference at Bethesda Naval Hospital, he pulled up his shirt and showed his 12-inch surgical scar directly to reporters and television cameras.
To diagnose this, you might press firmly under the patient's right ribcage and ask them to take a deep breath

This was synthesized in 1958 in Germany when attempting to engineer potent analgesic molecules from pethidine and methadone. Instead of pain relief, the molecule induced a distinct, immobile, trance-like state in laboratory animals while leaving them responsive to certain stimuli

While this medication was celebrated as a massive success in Europe almost immediately after its 1959 launch, an infamous 1950s clinical trial conducted in Manhattan reported that the medication was completely ineffective. This created a decades-long rift between European and American psychiatrists

This medication binds tightly to D2 dopamine receptors, contributing to the theory that overactive dopamine pathways drive hallucinations and delusions. Because of this tight binding, it can also cause acute dystonia, parkinsonism, tardive dyskinesia, and akathisia.
